task_description: The team must find a single fact buried in a specific book: the open-access UCL Press / JSTOR volume 'The Responsibility of Intellectuals: Reflections by Noam Chomsky and others after 50 years' (DOI 10.2307/j.ctv9b2xdv). The question asks: in the endnote attached to the second-to-last paragraph of page 11, a Wikipedia article is cited with an access date in November; give just the day of the month. The gold answer is the integer 4 (i.e., 'accessed 4 November ...').
final_vs_expected: produced 'cannot be determined' vs gold '4' — team declared the fact unobtainable rather than extracting the page-11 endnote it had nearly retrieved
primary_cause: WebResearcher repeatedly failed at the document-extraction step (PDF came back FlateDecode-compressed/unreadable, never OCR'd or decoded), so the access date was never recovered and the team converged on 'not established'.
mast_rationale: 1.3 (step repetition): the run becomes a sterile Critic<->WebResearcher loop from Turn 5 to Turn 25 (11 WebResearcher turns, 11 Critic turns), each re-stating 'not established' / 'not ready to finalize' with no new action — Turns 15,17,19,21,23,25 are bare 'Not established.' with no tool call. 3.1 (premature termination): Finalizer at Turn 26 ends with 'cannot be determined' even though the data exists and WebResearcher had at Turn 7 actually fetched the page-11 chapter PDF (got real %PDF-1.4 bytes) and merely failed to decode it. 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions): the team had no mechanism to escalate the extraction problem or to try a different tool (OCR, decompression, Google Books snippet) and instead spun until the message cap, the selector itself noting at Turn 24 'to keep the cycle going'.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher correctly identifies the book from the DOI (Crossref -> 'The Responsibility of Intellectuals'), tries the UCL PDF (HTTP 520) and many keyword searches, finds nothing containing the access date, and publishes a long honest message: book identified, page 11 not yet read. Turn 2: Critic accurately summarizes that the day is 'not provided anywhere' and asks WebResearcher to read page 11. Turn 3: WebResearcher tries JSTOR, fetches the chapter-6 intro landing page (title only), is 403'd on the stable URL, and brute-force searches 'accessed November 11/12/13/14' with no hits; publishes 'not found'. Turns 4-6: Critic and WebResearcher exchange near-identical 'not established' messages. Turn 7 (the pivotal turn): WebResearcher finds and fetches https://www.jstor.org/content/pdf/oa_chapter_edited/j.ctv9b2xdv.11 and DOES receive a real PDF (%PDF-1.4 ... iText ... FlateDecode streams), but the streams are compressed/garbled, it cannot read text, retries the identical fetch, and gives up: 'the date is not established'. Turns 8-25: a long degenerate loop — selector alternates Critic/WebResearcher; WebResearcher mostly publishes bare 'Not established.' with no tool calls; Critic republishes the same boilerplate 'not ready to finalize'; Analyst (Turn 14) adds nothing new. Turn 26: selector finally routes to Finalizer, which invokes a 'stall rule' and emits 'FINAL ANSWER: cannot be determined'.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is fundamentally a single-agent capability/tooling failure, not inter-agent misalignment. The decisive failure is at Turn 7: WebResearcher actually obtained the correct source document (the JSTOR open-access chapter PDF whose pages cover page 11 of the book — gold answer = 4) but its toolchain returned the raw, FlateDecode-compressed PDF byte stream, which it could not parse, and it had no fallback (PDF text extraction, decompression, OCR, or a Google Books / OAPEN snippet pass targeted at the endnote). Having failed extraction once, the system never tried a qualitatively different approach; the remaining ~18 turns are pure structural non-convergence layered on top: the selector keeps shuttling between Critic and WebResearcher, the Critic keeps issuing the same well-formed-but-inert demand ('WebResearcher must obtain and quote the endnote from page 11'), and WebResearcher keeps replying 'Not established.' without taking any new action. The Critic's demand is correct but un-actionable given the broken tool, so it functions as verification theater of the opposite kind — it correctly withholds approval but cannot unblock progress. The only mild misalignment is communication-loss/unreflective-publishing: WebResearcher never told the team that it had reached the actual PDF and that the blocker was specifically a decode/OCR problem ('I retrieved the chapter PDF but the text is compressed/unreadable'), which might have prompted the Analyst (who has run_python) to attempt PDF decompression/extraction. Instead WebResearcher flattened a rich, near-success state into the vague 'not established', so the Analyst (Turn 14) had no idea a parseable PDF was in hand and simply concurred.
reasoning_vs_published: The biggest private-vs-published gap is at Turn 7. Privately WebResearcher's reasoning shows it knew it had the document and that the blocker was extraction: round 2 reasoning 'The raw PDF I got wasn't readable, so I think extracting text from it might be necessary... check if I can access the chapter directly through an OCR method'; round 3 reasoning 'specifically page 11, as it might contain accessible text. I could use OCR for that, but the output I have seems truncated... if the text isn't clear from what I have, I'll need to let the user know I can't establish a precise answer.' Yet the PUBLISHED message collapses all of this to: 'I couldn't verify the day from the source I could access, so the date is not established from the available evidence.' The team never learns that (a) the correct chapter PDF was successfully fetched and (b) the only obstacle was OCR/decompression — information that the Analyst's run_python tool could plausibly have addressed. This is information-loss (2.4-adjacent) more than distortion: nothing false is stated, but the actionable detail is withheld. Downstream, the Analyst's Turn-14 reasoning ('I can't access the web right now... my team doesn't have it... I need to state what information is missing') shows it trusted the flattened summary and never considered parsing a PDF, confirming the lost signal was load-bearing. Elsewhere reasoning and publishing are consistent: the Critic's private reasoning ('only evidence is that the web researcher couldn't fetch page 11... it's unsupported') matches its honest published critiques, and the Finalizer's reasoning ('no established day, my final answer will need to be cannot be determined') matches its output — so the conclusion was faithfully reported, just wrong because extraction failed upstream.
